name: Plum blossom forehead makeup (meihua zhuang)

card.summary: A traditional Chinese forehead decoration, a painted or pasted floral mark between the brows, used to add a decorative focal point to the face.

quick.overview:
Huadian is traditional Chinese women's ornamental makeup, worn mainly on the forehead between the eyebrows. The plum blossom version, meihua zhuang, is linked in legend to a Southern dynasties princess.

It adds a decorative accent to the face and was widespread in the Tang dynasty. Today it appears with hanfu, in wedding styling and on television.
quick.how: The motif is painted on or applied as a pasted ornament or temporary tattoo; historical materials included gold or silver leaf, paper, feathers and pearls.
quick.risks: Minimal; adhesives and pigments can irritate skin.

lead: Huadian is a traditional Chinese women's ornamental makeup worn mainly on the forehead between the eyebrows, and sometimes on the cheeks, temples and dimples. It is also called plum blossom makeup or shouyang makeup [1].

Legend credits Princess Shouyang, daughter of Emperor Wu of Liu Song, whose forehead was marked by a plum blossom that others then copied [1]. It became widespread in the Tang dynasty, with more than ten plum blossom styles, grew fashionable with pearls in the Song, and declined in the Yuan [1].

chain: Apply a floral motif between the brows
Creates a focal accent on the forehead
angle.text: The motif adds a decorative accent at the centre of the forehead, usually in red, and can cover a mark or scar in one Tang legend.

paras: Painted figurines from a Warring States Chu tomb in Changsha suggest early forms [1]. In one legend, a plum blossom fell on Princess Shouyang's forehead while she napped and left a mark lasting three days; in another, the mark could not be washed off [1]. A Tang legend credits Shangguan Wan'er with covering a scar with a red plum, creating 'red plum makeup' [1].

Motifs include flowers, plum blossoms, butterflies, coins, peaches, birds and phoenixes [1]. Materials included emerald feathers, gold or silver leaf, paper, fish scales, pearls and dragonfly wings [1].
It is rarely daily makeup today, but appears in wedding accessories, television dramas and with hanfu, as painted designs or temporary tattoos [1].

timeline.event: Early forms suggested by painted figurines [1]
